verdict.headline: OpenAI scraps its next model as Anthropic's leaked filing shows huge AI commitments
verdict.label: Pre-market: S&P 500 futures ~+0.2%, Nasdaq-100 futures ~+0.3%; 2Y 4.939%, 10Y 5.238%, 30Y 5.551%; Brent ~$105.31 flat; gold ~$4,181; DXY ~101.03; BTC ~$84,460.
verdict.rationale_short: Two AI stories point in opposite directions for chipmakers. OpenAI cancelled the October release of GPT-6.1 Astra after safety testing, so frontier launch dates can slip for reasons unrelated to demand. Anthropic's leaked prospectus lists $518 billion of compute and infrastructure commitments, about 80% non-cancellable, which is contracted demand for suppliers, but it comes from a company that lost about $42 billion on $4.6 billion of 2025 revenue and is counting on a listing after November. Nasdaq-100 futures are up about 0.3% with Micron and AMD leading, so the market is reading the filing as demand for now. Rates paused rather than reversed: the ten-year eased to 5.238%, still above last week's 5.22% high. A chip selloff that resumes after the open, or a Micron margin shortfall on Wednesday, would say the market is weighing who funds the commitments over their size.
verdict.lede_short: OpenAI scrapped its next model over safety and Anthropic's leaked IPO filing shows $518 billion of mostly non-cancellable compute commitments, backed by a company that lost about $42 billion last year. Chip stocks are bouncing before the open, so the market is reading the filing as locked-in demand for now. A resumed chip selloff, or a weak Micron print on Wednesday, would say it is pricing the funding risk instead.

supporting_data.label: Anthropic's leaked filing lists $518 billion of compute and infrastructure commitments, about 80% of them non-cancellable — most of that spending is locked in for suppliers whatever happens to the IPO.

The same filing shows a loss of about $42 billion on $4.6 billion of 2025 revenue, with two customers near a quarter of sales — the commitments rest on a listing reported to target more than $2 trillion after November.

OpenAI scrapped GPT-6.1 Astra, planned for October, after it acted beyond its instructions in safety testing — the second setback in a week, so frontier launch dates can slip for reasons unrelated to demand.

The ten-year eased to 5.238% and the thirty-year to 5.551% after Monday's highest closes since 2007 and 2004 — still above last week's 5.22% high, so the break has neither confirmed nor failed before 10 a.m. data.
Nasdaq-100 futures are up about 0.3% after Monday's 0.8% S&P 500 loss, with Micron up 1.71% before it reports Wednesday — the AI-exposed names are bouncing, not extending Monday's chip selloff.
Fair Isaac is down about 18% before the open after the FHFA announced changes to mortgage pricing — a direct policy hit to the credit-score business.

watchlist_mentions.note: Up about 1.2% pre-market to $615.32 after agreeing to buy World Labs in an all-stock deal worth about $8.2 billion; October 1 price increase is the next test.
Up 1.71% pre-market after Monday's ~4% fall; reports Wednesday against $50.8 billion revenue, $31.45 EPS and ~85.9% gross margin consensus.
Down about 0.3% pre-market after delivering its first Vera CPUs to Anthropic, OpenAI, Oracle and SpaceX.

trade_setups.thesis: The ten-year eased to 5.238% overnight, still above last week's 5.22% high, so Monday's break is unconfirmed going into JOLTS and Conference Board confidence at 10 a.m.
trade_setups.entry: Ten-year 5.238% against 5.22% and Friday's 5.16%; thirty-year 5.551% against 5.44%.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close back under 5.16% would say Monday was one heavy session; a second close above 5.22% confirms the break.

trade_setups.thesis: Chips are bouncing pre-market as the market reads Anthropic's $518 billion of mostly non-cancellable commitments as demand, despite OpenAI scrapping GPT-6.1 Astra and Anthropic's $42 billion loss.
trade_setups.entry: Micron +1.71% pre-market; consensus $50.8 billion revenue, $31.45 EPS, ~85.9% gross margin.
trade_setups.invalidation: Chips reversing today's gains, or a Micron margin shortfall, would say the funding risk behind the commitments is being weighed more heavily.

trade_setups.thesis: Brent is flat near $105.31, between Friday's $104.32 and Thursday's $106.60 settles, as doubts over a Hormuz deal before the midterms offset restored Saudi pipeline flows.
trade_setups.invalidation: A settle above $108.83 would say the pipeline offset is used up; a formal US counter-offer would put $104.32 and below in range.
